journey.note: Tribunal award with 9% interest a year from the date of the petition. The head-wise table and the award date are not in the text.

Common judgment on appeals by the insurer and the claimant: the claimant's appeal partly allowed and the award raised, but interest cut from 9% to 6%. It gave Rs 2 lakh for pain and suffering and Rs 1 lakh for loss of amenities.
Claimant's appeal partly allowed: pain and suffering raised to Rs 10 lakh and loss of amenities and happiness to Rs 10 lakh; the 6% interest from filing was left unchanged.

precedent.holding: Answering the insurer's reliance on rulings giving only a token sum for amenities where earning capacity loss is taken at 100%, the Court held no straitjacket formula applies to pain and suffering or loss of amenities; each case turns on its facts: pain on hospitalisation, injuries and operations; amenities on the claimant's post-accident condition and ability to enjoy life.

extraction.title_anon: Man, 29, bank process supervisor, Karnataka (injury, coma)
extraction.family_summary: A 29-year-old bank employee suffered severe brain injuries in a road accident in January 2013, had several operations and remained in a coma, bedridden; his mother brought the claim for him. The tribunal awarded about Rs 94.37 lakh with 9% interest; on appeals by both sides the Karnataka High Court raised this to about Rs 1.25 crore in September 2020 but cut interest to 6%. In February 2022 the Supreme Court raised pain and suffering from Rs 2 lakh and loss of amenities from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 10 lakh each, a total of about Rs 1.42 crore with 6% interest, to be kept in long-term deposits for his use. It took just over nine years from the accident.
what_mattered: The long hospital stay, multiple brain surgeries and the claimant still being in a coma and bedridden years later led the Supreme Court to raise pain and suffering from Rs 2 lakh to Rs 10 lakh.

Relying on an earlier ruling, the insurer argued that once loss of earning capacity is paid at 100%, only a token sum is due for loss of amenities; the Court said there is no fixed formula and raised it from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 10 lakh for a person in a coma and bedridden for life.
The High Court's cut in interest from 9% to 6% a year was not disturbed.
